thread.title: China Import Tariffs Weighing On Apple Stock | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: China Import Tariffs Weighing On Apple Stock | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple stock dropped on Tuesday over concerns that the U.S. will place import tariffs on mobile phones and notebook computers made in China.
X In an interview with the Wall Street Journal posted late Monday, President Donald Trump raised the possibility of putting tariffs on tech products like laptops and Apple 's ( AAPL ) iPhones. The move would be the latest salvo in the growing U.S.-China trade war.
To date, Apple's China-made products have been spared in the trade fight. But the president's latest rhetoric could mean that iPhones, Mac computers and Apple Watches will be among the next products impacted.
Apple stock fell 0.2% to 174.24 on the stock market today .

Once the clear No. 1 most valuable company, Apple is at risk of falling to No. 2 behind Microsoft ( MSFT ). Apple has a current market capitalization of $826.8 billion. Microsoft has a market cap of $822.4 billion.
Tariffs Could Result In $1.5 Billion Hit To Apple Profits Trump's threat of a tariff on iPhones "could simply be a negotiating tactic ahead of the G20 Summit later this week," UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri said in a report. However, he noted that Trump has displayed a willingness to push forward with such actions.
Trump did not specify whether the tariff rate would be 10% or 25%, but said he thought the American public could "very easily" stand a 10% tariff.
UBS estimates that a 10% tariff could result in a $1.5 billion hit to Apple's earnings this fiscal year, which ends Sept. 28, 2019. That would translate to a reduction in earnings per share of about 33 cents, or about 2.5% of total earnings, Arcuri said.
If Trump imposes a 25% tariff, the impact to profits could be about $3.8 billion, or 83 cents a share, he said.
Arcuri's estimates assume the tariffs are implemented starting in January and that Apple would absorb the incremental costs rather than pass them on to consumers.
Wedbush Securities analyst Daniel Ives said the iPhone tariff threat is a "near-term overhang" on Apple stock.
"The Street will not be taking this news lightly as with the litany of bad news Apple (and its investors) have seen over the last month," Ives said in a report. "This tariff threat on iPhones out of left field from Trump will surely add to this white-knuckle period for Apple."
